title: El Niño heating up inflation
gist: Oxford Economics warns the intensifying, potentially record-worst El Niño plus the Subtropical Indian Ocean Dipole threatens African food output, and since food exceeds 50% of CPI in Ethiopia and Zambia, the inflation hit could exceed this year's oil shock, lifting 2027 inflation in most major African markets.

themes.theme: El Niño food-price inflation in Africa

insights.claim: The intensifying El Niño is projected to be the worst on record and, combined with the Subtropical Indian Ocean Dipole, poses severe risks to African agricultural output, livelihoods, external balances and energy markets, especially in eastern and southern Africa.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Weather shock transmits through food, FX/external balances and energy; watch East and Southern African sovereigns and currencies.
insights.locator: The intensifying El Niño weather event

insights.claim: Food weighs more than 50% in the CPI baskets of Ethiopia and Zambia, so rising food prices could have a larger inflationary effect there than this year's oil shock.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: High food CPI weights make these economies most exposed; expect inflation surprises and tighter policy risk.
insights.quote: Food carries a substantial weight in many African CPI baskets, exceeding 50% in Ethiopia and Zambia.

insights.claim: Most major African markets are expected to see higher inflation in 2027 than in 2026.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Delays in disinflation and potential rate-cut pushback across African markets in 2027.
insights.locator: As a result, rising food prices

insights.claim: Many sub-Saharan African countries have tabled disaster preparedness and response strategies including physical strategic food reserves and emergency financing, which may cushion the shock.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Mitigation reduces tail risk but adds fiscal/financing needs; watch emergency financing announcements.
insights.quote: Encouragingly, numerous countries across sub-Saharan Africa have already tabled disaster preparedness
